elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The new Affiliates provision extends the licences only "Upon written notice to Commerce One." It therefore does not provide the unconditional affiliate coverage contemplated by the preferred position.

elements.element: The licences extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No operative language extends any licence to Corio's contractors or other persons acting on Corio's behalf.

elements.element: Each fully paid-up licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 expressly grants a "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual" licence.

elements.element: Each fully paid-up licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Although Section 2.2 makes the fully paid-up licence perpetual, it does not make that licence irrevocable. The irrevocability language appears only in the separate fee-bearing licence in Section 2.1.

elements.element: If any subscription licence is granted, it may be terminated only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is granted in the supplied operative language; Sections 2.1 and 2.2 instead grant perpetual licences. The condition triggering this requirement is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 make the licences nontransferable except under Section 14.1. Section 14.1 permits specified M&A-related assignments, requires consent where the transaction involves a direct competitor, and refers only to "successors and permitted assigns"; it does not provide a general transfer right to all successors.

elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The added Affiliates provision states: "Upon written notice to Commerce One, the licenses granted to Corio under this Section 2 shall extend to Corio's affiliates."

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licences are nontransferable except under Section 14.1, which expressly permits assignment in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all relevant assets. A direct-competitor transaction requires consent, but the fallback does not expressly require consent-free transfer.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback through written-notice affiliate coverage and the existing M&A assignment provision, but it does not reach the preferred position because affiliate coverage is conditional, contractors are omitted, the fully paid-up licence is not irrevocable, and successor transfer remains limited by Section 14.1. The changes are not minimal and do not preserve unrelated commercial terms because new Section 2.10 adds a worldwide geographic-expansion mechanism, a no-additional-cost restriction, and an obligation concerning localized versions, none of which is needed for either licence-scope position.
